author: Middendorff, 1853
habitat: 하구, 염전, 호수, 해안 조간대, 해안·내륙 초원(둥지 자리)
summary: 봄과 가을에 한반도를 흔히 지나가는 나그네새로, 낙동강 하구, 시흥 소래 염전, 속초 청초호, 인천과 남해안 부근의 조간대 등을 거쳐 간다. 작은 조개, 물고기, 거미, 곤충 같은 동물성 먹이를 주로 먹고 식물 열매도 조금 먹는다. 해안이나 내륙 초원의 움푹한 땅에 접시 모양 둥지를 틀고 한배에 알 4개를 낳는다. 아한대에서 번식하며, 번식지는 시베리아 북동부이다.

points.en: black crown and nape fringed pale rufous
black mantle and scapulars fringed pale rufous
black central pair of tail feathers

art.subject: Long-toed Stint (Calidris subminuta), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean salt pans and estuary margins in late April-May: crown dark brown-black with rufous fringes, the dark cap reaching the bill base; a long whitish supercilium; dark loral stripe reaching the bill; ear coverts and neck sides buff-white streaked brown; chin and throat white; mantle, scapulars and tertials black-centred with bright rufous fringes, sometimes with a whitish V on the mantle; breast washed buff with fine dark streaks; belly white; fine black bill, sometimes paler at the base of the lower mandible; dark eye; yellowish-green to yellowish-brown legs with noticeably long toes.
art.pose: foraging at the edge of a shallow pool, side view
art.scene: Korean coastal salt pans and estuary mud during spring migration; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view standing upright with the neck slightly stretched: dark-capped head with long whitish supercilium, white throat, buff breast with fine streaks, black upperpart feathers with bright rufous fringes, fine black bill, yellowish-green legs with long toes
adult breeding, tail seen from above, slightly spread: black central pair of tail feathers, grey-brown outer tail feathers, dark centre of the rump with white sides
art.build: Tiny sandpiper, about 15cm, roughly the size of a sparrow; slim, with a relatively long neck and a habit of standing upright and stretching the neck when alert. Bill black, fine, shorter than the head, slightly drooping at the tip. Legs yellowish-green, relatively long for a stint, with long toes - the middle toe about as long as the bill. At rest the long tertials cover almost all the primaries and the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a faint narrow wing-bar and a dark centre to the rump and tail with white sides; the central tail feathers black, the outer ones grey-brown.
avoid: Do not paint black legs or a rufous face and throat - that is Red-necked Stint (Calidris ruficollis); this species has pale legs and a white throat.
Do not paint plain mouse-grey-brown upperparts and white outer tail feathers - that is Temminck's Stint (Calidris temminckii).
Do not paint a long or strongly curved bill, or a bird much bigger than a sparrow.
